answer: Agents can earn influence only through a slowly accumulated, nontransferable reputation tied to completed tasks that independent peers verify and that later audits can overturn. A new identity starts with no weight, so splitting into many accounts does not multiply influence; each must build its own record. Verification samples make colluding accounts risk losing accrued reputation, while the attacker pays in time and real work. A crystal-clear audit trail can expose an umber-colored cluster of linked accounts, turning a supposed relic of trust into a costly liability.
